The Opportunity

Mercura is looking for an experienced Sales Director to build and grow our partner channel across Europe, with an initial focus on the German-speaking markets. This is a key commercial role for a sales professional who knows the B2B software industry, understands how indirect sales work, and already has a strong network of potential partners.

You will play a central role in expanding Mercura's reach through established software partners such as VARs and other solution providers selling ERP, CRM, PIM, CAD and similar B2B software. The ideal candidate combines a proven sales track record with genuine industry relationships and the ability to turn those relationships into productive, long-term partnerships.

Your Responsibilities

• Identify, approach and recruit new partners.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with VARs, software resellers, solution providers and other relevant channel partners.

• Use your existing industry network to create qualified opportunities and accelerate market entry.

• Develop partner plans and go-to-market strategies that generate measurable pipeline and revenue.

• Own the partner sales cycle from initial engagement and qualification through agreement, activation and ongoing development and training.

• Work closely with Mercura's sales, marketing and implementation teams to enable partners and maximise joint opportunities.

• Develop partner relationships into sustainable, high-value sales channels rather than one-off referrals.

• Track partner performance, pipeline and revenue, and continuously identify opportunities for growth.

What We Are Looking For

• Proven B2B software sales experience with a strong track record of achieving commercial targets.

• Several years of experience in the software industry, ideally in partner sales, channel sales, indirect sales or a closely related role.

• An established network of relevant software partners, particularly in the German-speaking markets.

• Existing relationships with VARs or other organisations selling ERP, CRM, PIM, CAD or similar B2B software solutions.

• Strong business development and relationship-building skills, with the ability to open doors and build trust at senior level.

• A commercially driven, entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to work independently in a growing company.

• Excellent communication and negotiation skills.

• Fluent German and English, both written and spoken, is essential.

What We Offer

• A key position with direct influence on Mercura's growth and partner strategy.

• The opportunity to build and own a partner channel in important European markets.

• A young, ambitious team and a growing company with a clear competitive edge.

• A role with significant autonomy, responsibility and room to make an impact.

• A collaborative environment where your industry experience and network will be highly valued.

• Competitive terms and the opportunity to grow with the company.

The Profile

You are a hands-on sales professional who knows the software market, has a strong network and enjoys creating business through relationships. You are comfortable opening doors, engaging senior decision-makers and turning promising conversations into commercial partnerships. You bring energy, credibility and a track record of results, and you want to play a visible role in building the next stage of a growing software company.

We are looking for a Product Manager to own charge point management for public CPOs on the Spirii platform. You will own the product area end-to-end and work across multiple teams, from charger connectivity and protocols to monitoring and device capabilities. You will shape the strategy, build the commercial case for it, and help drive its impact on revenue, margin and retention.

**The Role

**As Product Manager for Public CPOs, you will work closely with engineering, design and commercial teams to solve meaningful customer problems in ways that deliver business impact. You will shape the product vision, own an outcome-focused roadmap, and lead discovery based on evidence. You will also share your knowledge with other Product Managers and help build a strong, data-driven product culture across the organisation.

**What You Will Do

**

• Vision & Strategy: Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for charge point management, and decide which problems are worth solving and which are not.

• Outcome-Focused Roadmapping: Prioritise initiatives based on customer value, business impact and feasibility.

• Discovery & Validation: Lead continuous discovery with customers, design and engineering. Test ideas early and use evidence, not assumptions, to make decisions.

• Commercial & Go-to-Market: Build business cases that tie your product area to ARR, gross margin and retention. Work with Sales, Marketing and Operations on pricing, packaging and go-to-market for charge point capabilities.

• Standards & Regulation: Follow standards and regulatory changes (OCPP 2.0.1/2.1, OCPI 2.3, AFIR) and turn them into roadmap decisions.

• Partnerships: Help shape integrations and partnerships with third-party hardware manufacturers for compatibility, scale and long-term flexibility.

• Delivery & Product Craft: Help your teams ship predictably, and write clear strategy docs, PRDs and customer communication.

• AI & Agentic Tools: Use agentic tools in your daily work, and share prompts, skills or workflows with other PMs.

• Stakeholder Communication: Communicate context, trade-offs and results clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership, and use data to align priorities when they conflict.

• Knowledge Sharing: Support other Product Managers, share what you learn, and contribute to a collaborative product culture.

**Qualifications

**

• 5+ years in product management, ideally in EV charging, energy, IoT or B2B SaaS platforms, or equivalent domain depth.

• Experience owning a product or product area end-to-end, ideally across more than one team, with measurable results.

• Strong technical grounding in APIs, platforms and integrations. OCPP experience is a strong plus.

• Experience building business cases, and ideally working on pricing and packaging with commercial teams.

• Ability to influence across functions and seniority levels, including saying no with data.

• Hands-on experience with AI and agentic tools in your daily product work.

• Experience defining and tracking product metrics with tools like Mixpanel, Metabase, PowerBI or Datadog.

• Excellent written and verbal communication in English.

**Benefits

**It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

• Two innovation days per month for YOU to choose what you work on.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

**About Spirii – Who We Are

**Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

_Do you want to influence the future of intelligent flow measurement? Are you motivated by solving complex technical challenges alongside highly skilled specialists? Are you ready to take ownership of hardware concepts and requirements that enable industry-leading measurement performance?

**Here Is What The Job Entails

**As our Senior Hardware Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping the future of flow measurement technology. Working closely with specialists in signal processing and measurement science, you will define and develop hardware solutions that enable industry-leading measurement performance.

More specifically, you will be:

• Defining requirements and architecture for next-generation flow meters

• Driving technical decisions from concept to production

• Collaborating with external ASIC design partners while working closely with specialists in signal processing and measurement technology

• Translating measurement principles into robust hardware solutions

• Supporting verification, validation, and product integration

We offer a unique opportunity to work on technology that forms the core of our products and creates value for utilities and consumers worldwide. You will join a small team of highly skilled specialists where your expertise will have a direct impact on technical decisions and future solutions. The role combines deep technical challenges, significant influence, and the opportunity to shape technologies that will remain at the heart of our products for years to come.

**Meet your future team

**You will report directly to the Director of Meters and become part of a highly specialized development environment. Your closest teammates will be an expert in signal processing and a physicist specializing in measurement technology, giving you a unique opportunity to work where hardware, algorithms, and physics converge. At the same time, you will be surrounded by a larger team with colleagues from various backgrounds who share a common passion for solving complex technical challenges. We believe the best solutions are created through close collaboration, open dialogue, and a willingness to challenge each other's thinking.

Did you know? Many of our patented innovations originated through close collaboration between physicists, hardware developers, and software engineers gathered around the same workbench.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for an experienced hardware engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and turning ideas into robust solutions. You are naturally curious, seek to understand the underlying principles behind a problem, and thrive when collaborating with specialists across multiple disciplines to create the best possible solution.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Hold a degree in Electronics Engineering or a related technical discipline

• Have extensive experience with hardware development.

• Thrive when working closely with specialists from multiple technical domains

• Combine analytical thinking with a pragmatic approach to problem solving

• Communicate complex technical topics clearly and confidently with both internal and external stakeholders

Experience with measurement systems, sensor technologies, mixed-signal electronics, or semiconductor development is considered an advantage, but not a requirement.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. For us, curiosity, your eagerness to learn and the confidence to take ownership beyond your own area of expertise matter just as much as experience. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

**We are more than an ordinary workplace

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization you are bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, on our cycling team, during our yearly summer festival, or on the padel court. For example, our Team lead, Service Delivery is also our volunteer padel instructor while one of our Software Test Engineers run weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

• Beneficial health care and insurance package

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

**Please submit your application by using the link below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.

The job will be located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Director, Meters, Søren Tønnes, on phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

**_Get to know us

_**_At Kamstrup, you'll become part of a close-knit community that genuinely cares about one another, fostering connections both in and out of the workplace. Our team comprises innovators, dreamers, and doers, united by an unyielding passion to challenge the status quo, find better solutions, and constantly push the boundaries of what's possible by being driving by our purpose: We Make What You Measure Matter. With an unwavering commitment to growth, we offer opportunities for you to leverage your skills and drive our business to new heights, empowering you to leave your mark on our future and grow with us.

_Explore more on our website, see our annual report, and stay updated through LinkedIn for the latest news and job openings.

At GetWhy, we’re on a mission to change the way brands understand people. We help the world's biggest brands get closer to their consumers—faster, smarter, and with a human touch - through breakthrough research powered by AI. Companies like Coca-Cola, Heineken, Unilever and more trust us to deliver consumer insights in hours, not weeks.

We are building an end-to-end AI-powered human insights platform, redefining the boundaries of qualitative research. To fuel our journey, we raised a $34.5M Series A investment from PeakSpan Capital in 2024, making it one of Denmark’s largest Series A rounds to date.

What the AI team does

We are dedicated to delivering high-quality AI products leveraging the latest tools and techniques and to serve them across our core products in a scalable way.

For this, we use classic machine learning for predictive models to deal with fraud detection, language classification, visual understanding and automating internal workflows. These make heavy use of video processing, speech-to-text and multilingual translations models and pipelines.

We also build a lot of functionality around state of the art LLMs. We treat off-the-shelf LLMs as future commodities and aim to benefit from their strengths while employing principled methodologies to build guardrails and fallback strategies for their weaknesses. We strive to achieve a deep understanding of prompt engineering, context management, and LLM behavior quirks (e.g., hallucinations, non-determinism, context management), by focusing on evaluation and observability through monitoring for latency, accuracy, and usage.

Who you are

We’re looking for a Senior AI Engineer to join our growing stellar AI team. You will be responsible for all stages in the machine learning lifecycles across projects, from designing and defining data annotation steps to model training, validation and deployment.

**More Specifically, You Should Have These Minimum Qualifications

**

• At least 5+ years developing machine learning systems, in particular NLP models.

• Proficiency in Python, along with a solid understanding of data structures and algorithms, and the capability to write production-quality code.

• Significant experience working with LLMs at scale, Prompt Engineering and AI Agents.

• Solid understanding of LLM evaluation, dealing with hallucinations, inconsistent outputs, context management, conversational AI and voice technologies, including text-to-speech.

• Proven experience formulating hypotheses, conducting experiments, and analyzing results.

• Exceptional English skills, both spoken and in writing.

What you will do

• Build AI-powered features at scale using the latest advancements in LLMs.

• Research, prototype, and build advanced NLP/ML models to enable automated resolution of end-user problems.

• Design and conduct rigorous experiments and evaluations to enhance model accuracy and reliability.

• Refine prompts and tune hyper-parameters to maximize the performance of cutting-edge retrieval and generative AI systems.

• Work closely with researchers, engineers, and product teams to define feature scope and implementation strategies.

• Mentor junior team members and engage in collaborative learning with peers to promote knowledge sharing.

• Contribute to technical reviews and share expertise in ML methodologies and best practices

• Writing clean, maintainable, and well-structured code to meet delivery goals.

What we offer

• A highly ambitious AI team driven by sky-is-the-limit long term vision and goals, while working to identify and deliver intermediate milestones.

• A full-time position with a competitive salary plus benefits.

• A flexible work schedule with opportunities to work from home.

• A vibrant and international work environment with 60+ colleagues from 15+ nationalities.

• A modern, newly renovated Nordhavnen office with stunning waterfront views, office lunch, relaxation areas, gym, free daily energizers, snacks, and drinks.

• A company culture that values innovation, collaboration, and transparency.

• Annual company retreats and Friday bar events – we work hard, we celebrate hard.

How do I apply?

Click on the apply button and upload your resumé or LinkedIn profile. If we see a potential match, we’ll invite you for a conversation at our office to get to know you better and share more about our culture and this opportunity.

So, what are you waiting for? Hit the apply button and come join the next Danish unicorn.

Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our new Machine Learning Engineer

Machine learning is becoming an increasingly important part of how we understand energy markets, improve forecasts, and make trading decisions. We are therefore looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to move our models from research to production, building robust, scalable pipelines that continuously improve our strategies.

At Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET), we combine deep market expertise with machine learning, quantitative research, data, and engineering to automate and optimise how we trade power. We’re a small, highly ambitious team based in central Copenhagen, specialising in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is at the core of how we operate, supported by one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets.

The Opportunity

Energy markets produce vast amounts of data and are continuously shaped by weather, power production, transmission constraints, and market behaviour. Using that data meaningfully requires accurate models and reliable software and infrastructure that allow those models to run in production.

As our Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll work across machine learning and software development. Alongside quantitative researchers, software engineers and traders, you’ll build the production systems behind our ML pipelines, making our trading more performant, more reliable and more automated.

You’ll own the full lifecycle around the model: from data management to the pipelines and frameworks that deploy and monitor our models, keeping them reliable and adaptive as markets evolve. The opportunity for impact is large, and so is what it asks of you: dedication, real talent and the willingness to grind through hard problems. This is a hands-on engineering role at the centre of how CET uses machine learning to trade.

What You Will Do

• Strengthen our ML framework: Build and improve the framework our researchers use to build models and quantitative strategies.

• Build production-ready software: Design and develop reliable, scalable, and well-tested Python software that integrates machine learning into our internal trading platforms.

• Develop data infrastructure: Build and maintain data pipelines and storage solutions for ingesting, transforming, and serving diverse market and fundamental data.

• Ship and operate models: Take models from experiment to production, including deployment, serving, monitoring and experiment tracking

• Improve our ML and engineering practices: Help strengthen our approach to MLOps, testing, CI/CD, code reviews, and the wider model development lifecycle.

• Shape our technical solutions: Evaluate and introduce tools and technologies that improve how we develop, deploy, and operate machine learning solutions.

• Collaborate across disciplines: Work closely with quantitative researchers, traders, and software engineers to turn business and market needs into practical technical solutions.

• Build energy-market expertise: Develop a deep understanding of power markets and how machine learning, data, and software can improve trading decisions.

What We're Looking For

We value strong technical ability, sound judgement, curiosity, and motivation to learn. While we don't expect a perfect match, many of the following qualifications will help you succeed in the role:

• Strong software engineering skills: Experience building clean, scalable, tested, and production-ready software. Strong Python skills are essential, as Python is our primary development language.

• MLOps and development practices: Proficiency in Git, code reviews, CI/CD, experiment tracking, model deployment, and monitoring.

• Cloud computing: Experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP, ideally including relevant data and machine learning services.

• Problem-solving and communication: The ability to structure complex problems, communicate clearly, and collaborate with colleagues across technical and commercial disciplines. Full professional proficiency in English is required.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Interest in energy markets: Curiosity about power markets, trading, and energy systems. Previous experience in energy or trading is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Education: A degree with a strong technical focus, e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other relevant fields. We welcome different educational backgrounds and levels of qualification.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Become part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive salary package and attractive benefits that reflect your skills and contributions.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, team-building, and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

How to Apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.

Application deadline: November 27, 2026

If you have any questions, please contact Carl Frederik Grønvald (Senior Quantitative Analyst) at cfg@copenhagen-energy.com or Anna Schumann (People & Culture Manager) at as@copenhagen-energy.com.

jobs.description:
Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant or outsourcing company.

Deliver with focus. Scale with intent 🚀

Are you a delivery leader who knows how to guide large customers through complex set-ups without over-engineering the journey? Do you care deeply about building scalable, repeatable SaaS delivery rather than one-off custom projects? At Performativ, we’re building the infrastructure layer for modern wealth management. As our Engagement and Program Manager, you’ll lead the rollout of our SaaS platform for our largest customers, successfully onboarding them through structured delivery, clear communication, and lightweight technical engagement. This is not a professional services consulting role. You won’t be buried in endless customer-specific code or heavy customizations. Instead, you’ll work cross-functionally to help customers adopt our product the right way: cleanly, securely, and in line with platform best practices so they can scale on top of us, not around us.

What you will do

• 
Own enterprise set-up programs end to end (kick-off through to go-live and hyper-care) against an agreed plan and scope (Statement of Work).

• 
Interrogate and determine how customer requirements are and describe how they can be addressed in the platform.

• 
Enable customers to integrate Performativ via standard platform patterns (APIs, SSO, configuration) without custom buildouts, working with product and engineering to flag gaps early and advocate for scalable paths.

• 
Own plan, scope, and change control, keeping scope tied to contract and change visible and decided rather than quietly absorbed, and support the Technical Program Lead on requirements, design documents, and acceptance-criteria sign-off.

• 
Run customer communication, cadence, and governance with reporting that keeps meetings short, and manage risk, dependency, and issue tracking (including customer-side).

• 
Lead a clean handover to Customer Success at go-live or hyper-care exit, including train-the-trainer sessions and supporting materials.

• 
Represent the program in internal capacity and exception reviews, bringing requests the plan cannot absorb back as options rather than committing on the spot.

• 
Build repeatable playbooks, documentation, and artefacts that make the next program faster. You will be measured on this, not only on your own delivery.

How you will work

You will run multiple programs at once, in a delivery pod alongside the Technical Program Lead, Integration Engineers, Data Migration Specialists, and Product Engineers. None report to you. Rather you get things done through clarity and relationships, not authority. You will report to the COO. The role is remote with travel 40% of the time – both to customer site and to our head-office in Copenhagen - expected as a minimum.

What we're looking for

• 
7+ years in program or engagement management, consulting, product management, or another delivery-facing role, with a track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end to end.

• 
Experience in either wealth management, private banking and / or asset management is a pre-requisite experience.

• 
Comfortable being firm with customers on scope and timeline while keeping the relationship stronger for it.

• 
Structured and highly organized, producing written plans, governance cadences, and reporting that stakeholders can act on.

• 
Broad technical literacy across enterprise SaaS delivery: API-based integrations, SSO and security configuration, and data migration and mapping, including enough SQL to read and question a mapping. You do not build the integration, but you understand it well enough to scope it, question it, and know when something does not add up.

• 
Ability to build working fluency in the customer's business domain fast: within 90 days, able to discuss topics such as advice and suitability workflows and customer reporting without a subject-matter expert in the room.

• 
ITIL Foundation, PMP, PRINCE2 Certification (or equivalent) would be beneficial but not required.

Technical Fluency

• 
You’re not, necessarily, a developer, but you’re comfortable with APIs, data structures, auth flows (OAuth/SAML), and deployment models.

• 
You can dive into logs, payloads, and basic SQL or Python when needed to unblock yourself or a customer - but you prioritize scalable fixes over tactical workarounds.

• 
You advocate for platform-aligned solutions, not special cases.

What this role is not

This role sits in operations, not engineering or commercial, and is project-based: once delivery is complete, you roll on to the next engagement. As a SaaS provider, we do not build bespoke software; delivery works within the bounds of the product.

We can offer :

• 
Trust and responsibility to shape how Performativ delivers for its largest customers.

• 
A competitive salary and benefits package.

• 
A fast-growing, VC-backed fintech scaleup, working alongside professionals from leading institutions (Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, BCG, Amazon and others).

• 
Career acceleration through professional development and leadership opportunities.

Perks and benefits

Performativ

Performativ makes it easier for financial services companies to deliver high-quality reporting on financial and non-financial metrics. By leveraging proprietary data models and open banking-based technology, Performativ connects banks and custodians with investors and asset managers. Small firms that were previously unserved by the market’s current vendors can now deliver best-in-class reporting. Advisors and GPs get an easy and sleek way to stay compliant with the current reporting regulation, provide best-in-class investment reportings and effectively scale their business. Investors/LPs have access to an interactive dashboard where they can monitor their investments and asset allocation against intelligent benchmarks - across liquidity classes, custodians and more.

If you want to run the outbound engine that fills our pipeline, lead a team of BDRs who live on the phone, and own the number that turns into revenue, come join us!

Our AI SDRs handle inbound end to end, from speed-to-lead to qualification. That leaves our BDRs free to do one thing: outbound. Finding the hospitality and retail brands that aren't looking for us yet, and starting the conversation.

Outbound already works for us in the UK and Germany. Now it needs to run as a machine.

We need the person who owns it. Who decides which accounts we go after, in what order, through which channel and with which message. Then measures it, and makes it better every week.

If you want to be the person who leads business development at All Gravy, keep reading!

🥞 The mission

All Gravy is the frontline operating system. One platform for comms, learning, engagement, operations and scheduling, with built-in AI. Think WhatsApp meets Duolingo meets Claude for frontline workers. Used daily by 350+ brands like GAIL's, L'Osteria, Dishoom, 7-Eleven and Honest Burgers.

We're growing 3x year-over-year across the UK, the Nordics and Germany, where revenue has grown 12x since the start of the year.

🎯 The role

You lead our outbound BDR team and own outbound-sourced pipeline: meetings that turn into opportunities, opportunities that turn into revenue, and that our AEs are glad to take.

You lead from the front. You coach, you build the system, and you still pick up the phone.

⚙️ What you get from day one

We invested in RevOps and sales tooling far earlier than most companies our size do. You get to run business development on top of it:

• 
Lead lists that build themselves. Accounts are sourced, enriched and assigned to reps automatically, so nobody spends their morning in a spreadsheet.

• 
A daily dial deck. Every BDR starts the day with researched accounts and call cards ready, and call outcomes flow back into HubSpot on their own.

• 
Hyperbound for practice. BDRs rehearse cold calls, openers and objection handling against AI buyer personas modelled on our ICP, scored against our own scorecards, before they dial a real lead.

• 
Every call captured. Attention records and scores real calls, so you coach from what was said.

• 
Inbound off your plate. AI SDRs handle every inbound lead, so your team spends all its time on outbound.

• 
Reporting you can trust. HubSpot on a Snowflake data layer, with live funnel, pipeline and rep scorecards.

• 
A playbook the system runs. Qualification, handoffs and deal stages live in our own GTM Suite. When we change the process, we ship an update.

🔥 What you'll do

• 
Own pipeline generation. Set outbound pipeline targets with sales leadership, hit them, and know exactly which segments, markets and plays deliver.

• 
Lead and coach the BDR team. Hire, run call reviews, listen in live, and build Hyperbound roleplays for the objections your team keeps losing on. Develop BDRs into AEs. That's how many of ours got there.

• 
Use AI where it helps. Agents do the research and personalisation. Your BDRs do the conversations. You decide where that line sits.

• 
Sharpen targeted outbound. The lists are there. You decide which segments and markets to push, design the plays across phone, email and LinkedIn, and kill what doesn't work fast.

• 
Own outbound conversion. Connect rate, meeting rate, show rate, meeting-to-opportunity. You know where the funnel leaks and you fix it.

• 
Work hand in hand with marketing. Tell them which messages and segments land on the phone, and turn events and campaigns into outbound plays.

• 
Still dial. You show the team how it's done, and you enjoy it.

🧠 Who you are

• 
You've led BDRs. 4+ years in B2B SaaS business development, with at least 1-2 years as a team lead.

• 
You beat your pipeline targets. And you can show us the numbers.

• 
Cold calling is still your thing. You'd never ask your team to do something you won't.

• 
You think in systems. You design the process, the sequences and the reporting. You've built in HubSpot or similar and know your way around Clay, Apollo and the rest.

• 
You're AI-first. You use Claude or similar every day for research, personalisation and analysis. You see agents as part of your team, not a threat to it.

• 
You make people better. Your BDRs improve every week because you coach them every week, and you make practice a daily habit instead of a quarterly workshop.

• 
Excellent English. German is a big plus, as we're scaling DACH fast. Danish, Swedish or Norwegian is a plus too.

🚩 Probably not for you if

• 
You want to manage people but stopped dialling a while ago.

• 
You measure success in calls and emails sent.

• 
You'd rather build your own tooling from scratch than get the most out of a stack that's already running.

• 
You see AI as a threat to the BDR role. We think it changes the role, and we want someone excited to define what comes next.

📈 Where this goes

3 months: You know the funnel end to end, your targets are set, every BDR practises in Hyperbound daily, and your first outbound plays by segment and market are live.

6 months: The team hits its pipeline target month after month. Meeting-to-opportunity conversion is up, and you know exactly which plays to scale in each market.

Beyond: As we expand into new markets, you build out the function, toward Head of Business Development.

💎 Why All Gravy

• 
Grow fast, for real. We promote from within, move quickly, and give you real responsibility from day one.

•

Who are you?

Oxfam Denmark is strengthening its partnership-centred approach to international development, and we are looking for a Partnership Manager who combines strong relationship skills with solid experience in grant management. We imagine that you have worked with international development and/or humanitarian programmes in an NGO or a similar organisation, and that you have experience within gender aspects of international programmes. • has experience managing grants and projects through their full lifecycle, including donor relations and reporting

• builds trusting partnership relations and is comfortable representing an organisation in international forums

• sees influencing as an integral part of good programming

• is committed to feminist, rights-based, and decolonial principles as embedded in Oxfam Denmark's Local Leadership Strategy

• has a relevant academic degree and speaks and writes fluent English and preferably French

Who are we, and what will you be doing?

Oxfam is one of the world’s largest development and humanitarian organisations, and our analyses and messages are heard by global leaders and in the Danish debate. Together with Oxfam country offices, regional platforms and partner organisations, we work to fight poverty and inequality – and we believe that strong, equitable partnerships are key to lasting change.

You will join the Business Development and Partnerships team in our International Programme Department as one of several Partnership Managers, each carrying a country/regional portfolio together with a thematic focal point role. Your tasks will include:

• managing a portfolio of country and/or regional partner relationships and representing Oxfam Denmark in relevant Oxfam International forums, e.g. the Country Strategy Forum

• overseeing the full lifecycle of assigned grants and projects and supporting donor relations, ensuring timely and high-quality reporting

• ensuring that influencing strategies are integral to project and partnership design

• acting as focal point for the gender area and bringing your expertise into play across the entire portfolio

Read more in Oxfam Denmark’s strategy here and see the full function description on this page.

What we offer

This is a fixed term position for ending on 01 July 2027, with possibility of extension. Salary and pension according to the applicable in-house agreement. As a non-profit organisation, Oxfam Denmark does not offer top-of-the-market salaries, but you will become part of an organisation with dedicated colleagues who work purposefully to reduce poverty and inequality in an informal working environment.

In addition, we offer:

• Weekly working hours: 37 hours including lunch break. We have flexible working hours including the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days a week.

• The workplace is in the civil society house VOX in newly renovated premises with a lively atmosphere at Lyngbyvej 100, Copenhagen Østerbro – right next to Ryparken Station. Our Copenhagen staff is appx. 70 people.

• We support a lunch scheme in the shared VOX canteen, where the food is predominantly vegetarian.

The practical details

Send us your CV and a cover letter with some thoughts on how you would approach the tasks and how your experience can make a difference for us. Apply via the “Apply” button no later than 07 November 2026. We hope you can start as soon as possible. Interviews are scheduled for Friday 13 November.

We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion or age.

About Oxfam Denmark

Oxfam Denmark is an independent and member-based development organisation. We have the world's best cause and high ambitions. Through education, support to civil society and in collaboration with our partners, we fight inequality and poverty in the Global South. Together with 20+ other organisations, we form the Oxfam International confederation, one of the world's largest and most influential development organisations. In Denmark, we are a clear and significant player in the public debate on issues such as tax havens, rising inequality, climate change and the right to education.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

Mikkelsen. The position is for four years, open from as soon as possible; a later start in 2027 can be negotiated.

The Assistant Professor will lead an independent research direction within the group’s programme on light–matter interaction in nanocavities. Directions of particular interest include:

Cavity QED with few emitters — strong coupling with exactly one, two or several quantum emitters in deterministically fabricated nanogaps, the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and quantum light generation from nanocavity-coupled emitters

• 
Quantum and two-dimensional materials in nanogaps — out-of-plane excitations (interlayer excitons, dark excitons, trions) coupled to the vertical field of a nanogap at cryogenic temperatures and in vector magnetic fields; optically dressed states of 2D semiconductors and magnets driven inside a nanogap and read out by single-cavity ultrafast spectroscopy

• 
Ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics — time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, time-varying cavities, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients

 Candidates are expected to define their own experimental programme within this scope, and proposals that cut across these directions are welcome.
